name: Family Money Dashboard
version: v2 · 2026-11-14 · statements-first setup · +1 step: keyboard 🎤 (24 Nov)
intro:
⚠️ BEFORE STEP 1 — check you are in a test copy. Look for the small “🧪 Test copy” mark on the screen. It means this app has never seen you, which is what the steps below expect. If it is missing and the app already shows your own information, you have opened your real app: go back to your list and tap this app's name again, rather than using a bookmark, your history, or an icon on your home screen.

The Family Money Dashboard gives a household three answers every month: what to spend, what to set aside for once-a-year bills, and how much comes from savings. You will look around an example family, fill in a missing yearly bill, answer the app's questions about unclear payments, see what is paid from each account, change a setting, check it remembers after a reload and with no internet, then start your own setup. All the money here is pretend. A short setup may be offered after the welcome tour, four questions you answer by tapping. Unless a step tells you to try it, tap “No thanks, just open it”.

steps.do: Look at the screen the app opens on.
steps.see: A card headed “Three answers, every month” with two buttons: “Set up ours” and “Show me an example family first”.
steps.tip: If a “What would you like to do?” start menu comes up instead, tap “This month” — that is the start menu, and it is right.

steps.do: Tap “Show me an example family first”.
steps.see: A yellow card says “👀 This is an example family, the Hendersons. Tap anything — it is pretend money.” Under the month name is a card headed “🧮 (last month) in three parts” with these rows: 1 · Spend each month, 2 · Save for later bills, Regular budget, Income $9,200, Left over, 3 · As needed this month.

steps.do: In that card, tap the “Income” row.
steps.see: A sheet says “Income: $9,200” and lists Pension $5,400 and Social Security $3,800. Tap “Close”.

steps.do: Tap the “2 · Save for later bills” row.
steps.see: A sheet headed “Bills once or twice a year”. The Travel card shows red words starting “Booked: Spring cruise ($3,900”. The “Home insurance (yearly)” card says “unknown” at the top right.

steps.do: In the “Home insurance (yearly)” card, type the number below into the “Yearly cost” box, then scroll down and tap “Save”.
steps.see: A message says “Saved.” The Home insurance card now says “$400 set aside” at the top right instead of “unknown”. Tap “Close” at the bottom.

steps.do: Scroll down to the card headed “🚩 Worth a look”.
steps.see: Among its lines is “Charged twice? RIVER GRILL, $86.40”, and at the bottom of the card a “Show … more” button.

steps.do: Scroll to the buttons near the bottom of the page and tap “❓ Getting to know you”.
steps.see: A sheet headed “Getting to know you · item 1 of …”. The card shows $120, the words “VENMO PAYMENT 1022”, and under the card “What was this?”.

steps.do: Tap “One-time purchase”.
steps.see: It moves on to item 2: $400, “ZELLE TO S MORGAN”, and asks “What was this?”.

steps.do: Tap “As-needed help for a person”, then tap “Nephew Sam”.
steps.see: Item 3: $1,200, “LAKEVIEW ACADEMY TUITION”. It asks “This looks like School costs paid by the 529 — right?” and the dark first button explains that a matching $1,200 came in from “COLLEGE SAV PLAN DISTRIBUTION”.

steps.do: Tap that dark first button. On the next item ($64.20, TOYSRUS ONLINE) tap “Not sure — skip for now”.
steps.see: Now $1,450, “MOUNTAIN ROOFING CO”, asking “This looks like Mountain cabin · Repairs & upkeep — right?”.

steps.do: Tap the dark first button. On the next item ($850, CHECK 1047) tap “Done for now” at the bottom.
steps.see: The sheet closes and you are back on the main screen.

steps.do: Tap “📋 Lists”, then tap “🤝 Nephew Sam · loan”.
steps.see: The list says “2 lines, $1,000 in all — a loan, to be paid back.” with $400 and $600 lines and a running total. Tap “Back”: the Lists sheet also shows “🎓 Paid by the 529” with $1,200 and “❔ Not sure yet (1)”. Tap “Close”.

steps.do: Tap “🔗 What’s paid from where”.
steps.see: A sheet with a card for “🏦 Joint checking ••4410” listing the bills that come out of it, starting with LAKESIDE MORTGAGE SERVICING $2,150.

steps.do: In the Joint checking card, tap “This account is closing”. Then tick the first box in the list.
steps.see: The sheet is headed “Moving everything off Joint checking ••4410”. After the tick, the line at the top changes from “0 of … moved” to “1 of … moved”, and the ticked line says “moved” with today’s date. Tap “Back”, then “Close”.

steps.do: Tap the card headed “🏡 Our household”.
steps.see: A sheet with three parts: “⏰ Coming due”, “🗝️ Where things are” and “📁 Documents”, each with an “Open … →” button. On a test copy the first two say “Nothing yet.” Tap “Close”.

steps.do: Tap the card headed “📈 Investments”.
steps.see: A sheet headed “📈 Investments: $539,400”, with a line chart, “🥧 Our mix”, the accounts one by one, and near the bottom “🌤️ Market weather” with a name in big letters. Tap “Close”.

steps.do: Tap the big “📝 Monthly report” button at the bottom of the screen.
steps.see: A sheet headed with last month’s name, starting with a card “🧮 The three answers”, then “📐 Biggest gaps”, “📅 Big-bill savings”, “🚩 Flags” and “📊 Net worth”. Tap “Close”.

steps.do: Tap “⚙️ Settings”, then tap “Monthly income: list each source and its amount.” Change the Pension amount from 5400 to the number below, and tap “Save”. Then tap “Close”.
steps.see: Back on the main screen, the Income row in the three-part card says $9,300.

steps.do: Reload the page (pull it down, or tap ↻ in Safari).
steps.see: The Income row still says $9,300.
steps.tip: If a “What would you like to do?” card comes up, tap “This month” — that is the start menu, and it is right.

steps.do: Turn on Airplane Mode. Tap “✏️ Our budget”, tap the ＋ next to Groceries, and tap “Save the budget” at the bottom.
steps.see: A message says “Budget saved.” — it works with no internet. Now turn Airplane Mode off.

steps.do: Scroll to the top and tap “Set up our own” in the yellow card, then tap OK.
steps.see: A small box first asks “Put the example family away and set up your own?”. After OK, a sheet headed “🔒 Your money stays with you”, saying everything is kept on this computer and nothing is sent to Daraja, with boxes to choose a passcode. (On a phone, a sheet “💻 Best kept on your home computer” comes first — tap “I only have a phone — set up here”.)

steps.do: Tap “Not now — no passcode”, then “Other ways to start”, then “Not yet — just ask me the questions”. On question 1, tap “Me and my spouse”, type the words below into the names box, and tap “Next”. On question 2, tap “Done for now”.
steps.see: The main screen shows a list headed “📝 Getting set up”, with ten steps, each with a circle to tick, and a “Start setup over” button under it. The bottom of the page says “Family Money Dashboard v4.6 · 2026-11-16”. Tap one empty circle: it fills with a ✓ and the count goes up by one. Tap it again to take it off.

steps.do: Scroll to the top of the main screen and tap “Start setup over”, then tap OK.
steps.see: A sheet headed “🔒 Your money stays with you”. Tap “Not now — no passcode”: then “How do you work?” appears, with three quick questions.

steps.do: Tap one answer in each: your device, “PDFs”, “Claude”, and for question 4 “I’ll do it myself, here”. Tap Next. On “Set up Claude first”, tap “Done — on to the folder”. Then tap “🧪 No folder yet? Try it with a sample one”.
steps.see: After a few seconds: “Your folder, connected” — a map with 📁 Family Money on one side, lines to each group folder, and from each group to its account boxes: Meadowbrook Checking ••3301 and Meadowbrook Savings ••3302 under Bank accounts, Capital One ••4417 and Discover ••8821 under Credit cards, then Venmo, Fidelity IRA (total $412,880), Grandkids 529, Mortgage Mr Cooper, and under Insurance: Home State Farm and Car Progressive. Green boxes were read in full. On a phone the map runs top to bottom.
steps.tip: Also try “None of these” for the AI: it should explain downloading CSV or Quicken files instead, or setting up Claude free. Say if any of it is unclear.

steps.do: On “Which year are we working on?”, leave “This year — January to December” chosen and tap “Use this window”.
steps.see: Three choices: this year (recommended), last year, or your own 12 months with a starting and an ending month. Then the “Put everything in one folder” page.

steps.do: Tap “Looks right — next”.
steps.see: A card headed “Found in your statements”, numbered 1 of 9, asking “Two homes?”, with two power companies listed under it.

steps.do: Tap “👆 Next: Meadowbrook Checking” at the bottom. First comes “Are these yours?”: tap one category to strike it out, type “Pets” under “Add one that’s missing” and tap “＋ Add it”, then tap “These are ours — start sorting”. Then a payee comes up with its statement words, how many lines, and the app’s guess already picked. For one payee, pick a different category and tap the button. For another, pick “＋ A new category…”, name it, and tap Save. For a third, tap “🔍 Look into later”. Back on Sort each account, tap “🔍 To look into” and check it is listed.
steps.see: Every category, grouped, each with a ✓; a struck-out one shows ✗ and is left out of the list after. Pets is in the list. Then one payee at a time, counted as “1 of N”; one answer sorts every line from that payee. The list starts with ＋ A new category…, then “Picked most”, then “All, A to Z”. A payee with a few different amounts says “These look like N different charges” — “Sort each one” lets you name each, e.g. Hulu. A single charge has “✂️ Split it across categories”. “✎ Rename it” renames the chosen category. On a computer, typing a letter jumps through the categories starting with it.

steps.do: Tap the guess on each of the rest until the account says it is sorted, then tap “👆 Next:” for each account, until the bottom button says “All sorted — on to the questions”. Then, on any account in Sort each account, tap “a spreadsheet” under its button.
steps.see: Each account ends with a count: payees sorted here, lines that sorted themselves, and card payments set as money moving. The spreadsheet is still there as the other way, with a drop-down in the yellow “Your category” column.

steps.do: Tap “All sorted — on to the questions”. On each one, tap the first choice, until “All answered ✓”. Then tap “See where the money went”.
steps.see: One question at a time — checks, cash, money sent to people — with a note to look in the checkbook and a button to ask someone by text. Then a picture: each account on the left flowing into its categories on the right, with totals.

steps.do: Tap “Looks right”. In the setup list, tap “🏡 A few questions about your household”, tap Next on each question, then the last button.
steps.see: For each kind of spending: how often it comes (every month, up and down, once or twice a year, one-time, as needed). Then “Here is a normal month” with the budget.

steps.do: Tap “Make this our budget”. On the main screen, tap “⬇️ Budget spreadsheet” and open the file.
steps.see: A budget laid out in three parts — the month at the top, Part 1 spend each month by group, Part 2 save each month for later bills, Part 3 as needed — with totals that update when a blue number is changed. A second tab, Reclassified, lists every line sorted.

steps.do: On the main screen, use the › arrow to get to this month. In the “in three parts” card, tap “Still safe to spend”, then close it and tap the 🙏 giving line and save a goal.
steps.see: Safe to spend shows the plan, minus what is spent, minus the bills still to come out this month, with each bill and its usual day. The giving line then reads “$X of $Y” with a bar and a percentage.

steps.do: Tap “🔁 Subscriptions”. Go through them; on one, tap “Cancel it”, then Next.
steps.see: Any subscription whose price rose says “📈 Went up” with the old and new price. After Cancel it, a ready-made cancellation message appears with Copy the message and Have my AI write one. Nothing is sent.

steps.do: On the main screen, in “💬 Ask about our money”, tap “Can we afford a new car?”. Read the words it will send and tap “Send it”. Answer each question it asks by tapping a choice or typing, until the answer comes.
steps.see: A line under the box says only totals go to the AI, never statements, account numbers or payee names. The AI asks one thing at a time (price, money down, trade-in…), then gives an answer that ends “A helper, not a financial advisor”, with a button such as “➕ Add … to the yearly bills”. If the AI connection is busy, it says “The AI didn’t answer” with “Try again”.

steps.do: If there is a yellow “Heads up” card at the top of the main screen, read it and tap its first button (“✨ Make a plan”, a shop-around script, or “Keep it”). Then tap “✅ Do this” or “Got it”.
steps.see: Only one heads-up card at a time — a yearly bill coming up short, a policy renewing, or a new subscription. After you deal with it, it goes away and the next one (if any) shows. “⏰ Remind me” saves a calendar file for your phone.

steps.do: Tap “📋 Lists”. If there is a “👯 Charged twice?” button, tap it. On one charge tap “It’s a mistake”, then tap “Change” and tap “Both are right”.
steps.see: One list of every charge that may have gone through twice: the payee, the amount, both dates and the account. Each answer shows straight away on the same screen, and the list stays where it was. “Change” brings the two buttons back.

steps.do: Open any screen — Settings, a list, or the budget questions — and tap the round ✕ at the top right. In the budget questions (“The budget · kind 3 of …”), tap “🔎 What makes up …?” first, then “Back”, then ✕. Then start the budget again.
steps.see: Every screen has the ✕, even after you scroll down, and it takes you straight back to the main screen. “What makes up” lists every payee in that kind, biggest first, then each payment. Starting the budget again picks up at the same kind, with a “Start from the top” link.

steps.do: On the main screen, look at the top box “Our money”. Tap each of the three dials, then “Safe to spend”, “Net worth”, one row under “Needs you”, and each of the four blue buttons at the bottom. Close each screen with ✕.
steps.see: One sentence says whether the month is under or over income, with one button under it. Three dials: Income in, Spent and Yearly bills. Below them: Safe to spend, Net worth, Coming up (bills only, next 30 days) and Needs you. Every one of them opens a screen about that thing.

steps.do: Sort a credit card (the Sort each account screen, then a card). On three payees in a row, tap the big ✓ at the bottom. Then tap one of the category buttons under the question, then 🎤 Say it and say “dining out”. Tap “💬” at the bottom on one payee.
steps.see: Each payee shows in a box at the top with a web-search link, then “This looks like … — right?”. The categories you used last appear as buttons. After three ✓ on the app's own guesses, a green “⚡ Accept the app’s guess for the other …” button appears and shows them all as a ticked list first. 🎤 picks the category you said (or says it heard nothing like it). 💬 moves that payee to your spouse's questions.

steps.do: On the main screen, tap “🧭 If I’m away”. Read it, then tap “🖨️ Print it” (you can cancel the print window).
steps.see: What’s due in the next two months, with the monthly bills and which account pays each; what’s normal each month; every account with its balance; who to call (the CPA and advisor from setup). The print shows the same page.

steps.do: Now the videos. This app has 3. Open each one and watch it right through, sound on: Explain it to me — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=familydash&mode=firsttime  Watch it work — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=familydash  Train me — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=familydash&mode=train
steps.see: Each one talks without stopping — no long silences, no sentence starting again. The screen behind the words changes to show what the voice is talking about, and a pointer lands on the thing it names. If the voice talks about a button that is not on the screen, that is a real fault — say which video and which sentence.

steps.do: Last, the shop page everyone sees: https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/ — find Family Money Dashboard on the “Your household” shelf and read its card.
steps.see: The name and the one-line description match the app you just used. The card says Coming soon, and that is right: it joins the store when it passes testing. Nothing on the card promises something the app does not do. If the card and the app disagree, the card is the fault — say which bit.

steps.do: Tap into any box where you type (a name, a note, a to-do). Look beside the box for a small round 🎤 pop-up. Then tap the 🎤 on your phone’s keyboard and say a few words. Do it three times in a row. If this app has no box to type in, skip this step and say so.
steps.see: No floating round 🎤 button sits beside the box, and the keyboard’s 🎤 writes your words all three times, not just the first or second. A few apps have their own 🎤 button built into the screen (Feedback Studio, Rafiki, One Thing, Business Manager, In My Own Words). That is meant to be there. A fault is a floating 🎤 beside a box, or the keyboard 🎤 stopping after one or two tries. If it stops, tell us which time, and your phone (iPhone or Android).
